A.1.6 References
Citations are important in scholarly writing to show readers that you have performed the appropriate 
research. By listing your sources, you acknowledge and give credit to other researchers for their 
work and ideas and avoid plagiarism. 
A minimum of 2 peer-reviewed research articles must be cited in the text of each laboratory report. 
Research articles cited in text must be also presented in the references section of your report. At 
least one of these articles should be an original research study, i.e. summarizing a research 
experiment and containing introduction, methods, results, and discussion sections.
Follow the citation format outlined in the APA 7th edition for your in-text citations and your reference 
page. As an example, consider the article (Figure A.1) by Asker Jeukendrup (on PubMed Central here):
REVIEW ARTICLE
Training the Gut for Athletes
Asker E. Jeukendrup1
Sports Med (2017) 47 (Suppl 1):S101–S110
DOI 10.1007/s40279-017-0690-6
Figure A.1: Peer-reviewed journal article on sports nutrition by Asker Jeukendrup. The first page of a journal 
article typically contains the information you need to create a citation. 
From the first page, we can obtain the elements required for the citation for your reference list:
•	 Author - Asker E. Jeukendrup
•	 Publication Date - 2017
•	 Publication Title - Training the Gut for Athletes
•	 Publication Source - Sports Med 47 (Suppl 1): 101-110. DOI 10.1007/s40279-017-0690-6
